<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
**The total number of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases in [[Canada]] surpasses 100,000, with 8,266 deaths recorded. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-canada/canada-hits-100000-coronavirus-cases-major-challenges-remain-idUSKBN23P3AX (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[India–Nepal relations]]
**The upper house of [[Nepal]]'s [[Federal Parliament of Nepal|parliament]] approves a new map for the country which includes territories controlled by [[India]]. The map requires the approval of [[President of Nepal|President]] [[Bidhya Devi Bhandari]]. India opposes the move, saying that the decision to include [[Limpiyadhura]], [[Lipulekh]] and [[Kalapani territory|Kalapani]] is not based on evidence or historical facts. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/nepal-parliament-approves-map-includes-land-india-claims-200618074902407.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2020 United Nations Security Council election]]
**After a second round of voting, [[Kenya]] defeats [[Djibouti]] in becoming a non-permanent member on the [[United Nations Security Council]] starting in 2021. They will join four other newly-elected members, [[India]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], [[Norway]] and [[Mexico]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/kenya-defeats-djibouti-win-seat-security-council-200618194420819.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*''[[Department of Homeland Security v. Regents of the University of California]]'', [[Immigration to the United States]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United States|U.S. Supreme Court]] rules in a 5–4 decision that the rescission of the [[Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals]] (DACA) policy was "arbitrary and capricious" under the [[Administrative Procedure Act (United States)|Administrative Procedure Act]] (APA) and reversed the order rescinding it. [[Chief Justice of the United States|Chief Justice]] [[John Roberts]] casts the deciding vote, along with the four liberal Justices. [https://www.npr.org/2020/06/18/829858289/supreme-court-upholds-daca-in-blow-to-trump-administration (NPR)]

;Politics and elections
*Aftermath of the [[2020 Burundian general election]]
**[[Évariste Ndayishimiye]] takes office as the [[President of Burundi]], following the sudden death of his predecessor [[Pierre Nkurunziza]], his inauguration was advanced to June 18. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/ndayishimiye-sworn-burundi-president-200618103042383.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Brazil]]'s [[Ministry of Education (Brazil)|Education Minister]] [[Abraham Weintraub]] announces his [[resignation]]. He did not give a reason; it is believed to be due to derogatory remarks he made about the [[Supreme Federal Court]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-brazil-politics-weintraub/brazil-education-minister-quits-after-antagonizing-supreme-court-idUSKBN23P3FM?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Science and technology
*[[Censorship in the United States]], [[Donald Trump on social media]]
**[[Facebook]] removes a post condemning [[Antifa (United States)|antifa]] by [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s [[Donald Trump 2020 presidential campaign|re-election campaign]], stating the post's symbol for the group was similar to [[Nazi concentration camp badge#Single triangles|the one used by the Nazis]] to identify political prisoners. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53098439 (BBC News)]
*[[Prime Minister of Australia|Australian Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] says "all levels of government", as well as essential service providers and businesses, are being targeted by a sophisticated state-backed [[cyberattack]]. Morrison did not say which state is behind the attack. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-australia-46096768 (BBC News)]

;Sports
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in the State of Palestine]]
**Local sporting events, such as [[equestrianism]], resume in the [[Gaza Strip]] today. As of tomorrow, [[Association football|football]] competitions will be played without spectators. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-palestinians-sport/gaza-horse-riders-compete-again-as-coronavirus-curbs-eased-idUSKBN23P366?il=0 (Reuters)]
*In Germany [[Matthias Grosse]] is appointed as president of the national German speed skating association, {{ill|Deutsche Eisschnelllauf-Gemeinschaft|de|lt=DESG}}. This is seen by national and international media as very remarkable as controversial person and parter of drug banned speed skater [[Claudia Pechstein]]. [https://www.spiegel.de/sport/wintersport/eisschnelllauf-matthias-grosse-ist-neuer-praesident-der-general-a-45048474-ac26-4d6b-a5df-047853e87a31 (''Der Spiegel'')] [https://www.volkskrant.nl/sport/in-de-duitse-schaatswereld-wordt-een-trumpiaanse-putsch-van-claudia-pechstein-gevreesd~b9990699/ (De Volkskrant)] [https://www.deutschlandfunk.de/neuer-eischnelllauf-praesident-matthias-grosse-eine.890.de.html?dram:article_id=478996 (Deutschlandfunk)]
